summary: Frontend-only testing of 'Gatilhos de Entrada' feature in SinaisTab.jsx ('Em Construção' tab). All 8 requested scenarios executed against live preview URL. 7/8 fully PASS; 1 minor ambiguity on LIMPAR scoreboard behavior (see notes). Signal detection, filtering by dominant color, hit/miss counting, and edge cases all work correctly.

tests_executed.name: H. LIMPAR resets signal; scoreboard persists
tests_executed.details: Signal correctly cleared to 'Mínimo 3 giros para detectar padrão'. Scoreboard was NOT reset by LIMPAR (stays WIN:1 / RED:1). The review request wording 'resets the signal and scoreboard display correctly' is ambiguous — code (limpar() only calls writeGiros([])) intentionally preserves scoreboard across history clears (typical cumulative scoreboard behavior). If main-agent intent was that LIMPAR should also reset scoreboard, then setScoreboard({wins:0,reds:0}) must be added to limpar().

action_items: CLARIFY (product decision): Should the LIMPAR button also zero the WIN/RED scoreboard, or is preserving it (cumulative across history clears) the intended behavior? Currently scoreboard persists. If reset is desired, add setScoreboard({wins:0, reds:0}) inside limpar() in SinaisTab.jsx line ~175.
critical_code_review_comments: SinaisTab.jsx is 493 lines — near the 700-line soft limit. Consider extracting GatilhoCard, RefAnalysisCard, HistoryCard, Keyboard, CounterHeader into separate files under components/sinais/ for maintainability.

Signal effect (lines 128-166) uses signalRef + prevGirosKeyRef to detect 'new' spins. Logic correctly handles: (a) new number added, (b) undo/clear (giros shrinks → updateSignal(null)), (c) hit vs miss branching. Verified working across all 8 scenarios.
detectTrigger (lines 43-55) correctly requires ≥2 consecutive same categories before a differing category. Edge cases (2 numbers, 3 different) properly return null.
getFilteredByColor uses dominantColor==='red' ? isRed : !isRed — correctly excludes 0 from BAIXO/MEDIO/ALTO ranges (ranges are 1-12/13-24/25-36).

Dominant color tie-breaker: r > b uses strict '>', so equal counts → 'black'. In GatilhoCard: r > b ? 'VERMELHO' : 'PRETO' — same. Consistent. But note: at 0 giros both are 0 and it defaults to PRETO — that's fine because signal is guarded elsewhere.
Recharts console warnings ('width(0) and height(0)') appear on other tabs during navigation — pre-existing, unrelated to this feature.
401 errors visible at initial page load — likely pre-login auth check (expected), not a functional issue.
